title: SURGE-Ahead Dashboard and AI Pilot Study
summary:
For patients of advanced age, it is beneficial if physicians without expertise in geriatric medicine are supported in their treatment by a geriatrician. Unfortunately, due to a shortage of geriatricians, this has not yet been possible on a nationwide basis. 
That is why the SURGE-Ahead project developed a special software – the SURGE-Ahead Application (SAA). This software helps doctors in surgical departments to provide better care for older people. It displays information on typical problems associated with old age that should be taken into account in relation to surgery and provides recommendations for the best possible follow-up care. It also uses artificial intelligence (AI). The data for this comes from various sources, such as questionnaires and tests, laboratory values, and sensors that measure mobility after surgery.
This software is now being tested in a study in three departments at Ulm University Hospital: trauma surgery, general and visceral surgery, and urology. The study will examine whether the software can be used effectively in everyday clinical practice and whether it really helps.
Approximately 300 to 350 patients aged 70 and over who are admitted to hospital for surgery are eligible to participate. Participants will be examined or interviewed during their hospital stay and three months and 15 months after discharge.
conditions: Geriatric-specific comorbidity in surgical procedures (emergency or elective) in trauma, hand, plastic, and reconstructive surgery, general and visceral surgery, or urology
Care deficit / lack of continuity of care (COC) after discharge

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• ISAR (Identifying Seniors at Risk) score ≥ 2
• Inpatient admission for surgery
• Surgery has not yet been performed
Exclusion criteria:
• Patients receiving palliative care (life expectancy < 3 months based on clinical assessment by the attending physician)
• Patients who are unable to give consent and who have no legal guardians or authorized representatives
• Assessments cannot be carried out due to limited communication skills (e.g., due to a lack of language skills)
• Length of inpatient stay < 3 days
